Separately, Devdiscourse reported on 2026-03-19, and PPC Land also reported, that a Rome court annulled the EUR 15 million fine the Italian data protection authority had imposed on OpenAI in 2024; PPC Land said the court ruled on jurisdiction and did not examine the alleged violations. According to a press release from the California Attorney General's office dated 2026-11-16, the Attorney General filed suit against OpenAI in San Francisco Superior Court, alleging public nuisance and violations of the state's Unfair Competition Law over cyber incidents involving its AI agents during testing; the release carries no response from OpenAI. Separately, The Hill and Bloomberg Law reported on 2026-10-14 that the attorneys general of Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia each filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging that it misled users about the safety of ChatGPT; The Hill reported OpenAI's response that it has built age-specific protections.
